dict.string: Flare uses your location to work out which country or state you are in, so it can show the right emergency numbers, and to find nearby hospitals, police stations, fire stations and pharmacies. Searching nearby places sends your approximate location to Apple Maps. Flare does not send your location to its own servers.

With Background protection on, Flare keeps location on at low accuracy so it can keep running in the background: fall detection keeps watching with the phone in your pocket, and official alerts for your area (such as flood warnings) are checked and sent as notifications. Looking up US weather warnings sends your position, rounded to about 100 m, to the US National Weather Service. Flare has no servers of its own.

Flare uses the motion sensor to notice a hard fall, only while Fall detection is turned on: while Flare is open, or in the background when Background protection is on. Motion readings stay on your phone and are never saved.
